item: Define whether the model predicts binding, presentation, immunogenicity, vaccine triage, or benchmark ranking.
Report source dataset, study, patient, assay, date/year, HLA typing method, and candidate-generation route when available.
List all public predictor scores used as features, comparators, filters, or product assists.
Report exact peptide and exact peptide-HLA overlap between train, test, public corpora, and comparator training data where available.
Report near-peptide, mutation-pair, source-window and TCR motif overlap where available.
Build retrieval, scaling, imputation, calibration, feature selection and thresholding inside train folds only.
Include exact, near, source/study, HLA allele/supertype, time/assay and retrieval-clean splits when feasible.
Use AUPRC, top-k precision, enrichment over prevalence and recall@k as primary metrics.
Report AUROC as secondary, with prevalence baseline.
Report Brier, ECE and calibration plots.
Report OOD flags, abstention coverage, and precision after abstention.
Describe whether negatives are true non-immunogenic, untested, assay-limited, or unlabeled.
Report per-source prevalence, feature shift, score shift and source-heldout performance.
Report per-HLA and HLA-heldout/supertype-heldout performance.
Report bootstrap or repeated split uncertainty for top5/top10.
Publish model card with intended use, forbidden use, inputs, leakage controls and known failure modes.
Separate internal validation, locked retrospective tests, source-heldout stress tests, and external prospective validation.
Report performance at realistic assay/manufacturing queue sizes.
Do not train on public predictor scores when those predictors are clean comparators.
Provide split manifests, row identifiers, seeds and scripts.
